attrs.title: Thinking recursively
attrs.subtitle: Solve a problem by solving a smaller copy of it.

content.text: function calls itself on a smaller input. Every correct recursive function has two parts:
An input small enough to answer directly, with no further call. It stops the recursion. For factorial: 0! = 1.
Express the answer in terms of the same problem on a
input, so that every chain of calls reaches the base case. For factorial: n! = n × (n − 1)!

def factorial(n):
    if n == 0:                       # base case
        return 1
    return n * factorial(n - 1)      # recursive case

print(factorial(4))   # 24

def merge(left, right):
    result = []
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:
            result.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            result.append(right[j])
            j += 1
    result.extend(left[i:])
    result.extend(right[j:])
    return result
